title.narrative: Integrated Health, and Nutrition services for crisis-affected communities in Jowhar district.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project is part of the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Flagship Initiative under Standard Allocation 2 (SA2 2025), targeting Jowhar District in Hirshabelle State. Between October and November 2025, ASEP (a National CSO) facilitated CE sessions in 10 villages across Jowhar. Each village underwent a three day participatory cycle involving storytelling, resource mapping, issue ranking, capacity mapping, and validation with Area Based Coordination (ABC) members. This process produced detailed Community Action Plans that reflect the lived experiences, capacities, and priorities of diverse groups including women, youth, elders, minority clans, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtThe CE findings highlight recurrent flooding, crop loss, and service gaps as the most pressing challenges. Health services were prioritized in six villages, with communities calling for the rehabilitation or expansion of health facilities, provision of medicines, and maternal and child health support. The project will directly respond to these communities validated priorities by implementing integrated lifesaving interventions across Health and Nutrition, while reducing risks of exclusion, exploitation, and abuse.ltbrgtThe project will target five (5) flood-prone riverine villages including Barrow-weyne, Bulo-Waraay, Bayaxow, Lebiga, and Shiidla Bari, reaching an estimated population of over 35,580 people (11029 woman 8895 men, 8539 girls, 7116 boys). Activities will focus on the immediate restoration of life-saving health and nutrition services through outreach and static service delivery, while supporting early recovery by re-establishing functional primary health care at community level.ltbrgtOur interventions will include the rehabilitation, construction and equipping of three (3) health facilities and two outreach service points across the target locations in the District to restore access to medical consultations, maternal and child health services, and treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM). Communities prioritized strengthening Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and integrated management of childhood illnesses, which will be addressed through facility based services and outreach. with deliberate inclusion of women, youth, minority clans, and persons with disabilities to ensure equitable access. By grounding these activities in community validated action plans, the project will strengthen local ownership, reduce health risks, and build resilience, while contributing directly to the 2026 Somalia Humanitarian Response and Needs Plan (HRNP) and demonstrating the Flagship Initiative’s community driven model of humanitarian action.ltbrgtThe project will adopt a community first approach, ensuring continuity of engagement throughout implementation. Communities will remain actively involved in monitoring progress, adapting plans, and sustaining dialogue with ABC structures. Protection and inclusion principles will be mainstreamed. A baseline assessment will be conducted at the outset to capture the current health and nutrition status of communities in the five target villages (Lebiga, Barrow Weyne, Shiidla Bari, Bayaxow, and Bulo Waraay). This baseline will provide evidence on service gaps, community priorities, and existing coping mechanisms, ensuring that interventions are tailored to local realities and measurable progress can be tracked over time. Finally, an endline assessment will be conducted at the conclusion of the project to measure changes in health and nutrition outcomes, assess the effectiveness of interventions, and capture lessons learned.ltbrgtlt/pgt
